For T (u, v) = (e cos v, e sin v) on R , which statement is correct?
(A) The Jacobian vanishes everywhere.
(B) T has a differentiable local inverse at every point but is not globally one-to-one.
2 2
(C) T is a bijection from R onto R .
(D) The Jacobian changes sign when v changes sign.
(E) T has no local inverse at any point.

solution.text:
2u 2 2 2u
The Jacobian determinant is e (cos v + sin v) = e > 0, so the inverse function theorem
applies at every point. But T (u, v + 2π) = T (u, v), so global injectivity fails. Its image is the
punctured plane. Nonzero Jacobian is a local criterion.
